https://thecolu.mn/4341/slovakia-will-no.text: Politics August 2, 2026 Slovakia Will Not Recognize Same-Sex Marriages Abroad The Slovak government does not intend to recognize same-sex marriages or civil partnerships concluded in another EU country. The Slovak constitution defines “marriage as a union between a man and a woman,” Interior Minister Matus Sutaj Estok explained in a video published on social media on Friday. He noted that this fact remains unchanged even if the union was legally established under the jurisdiction of another country. “If someone desires such a fundamental change, the only path is through a constitutional amendment, not through evasion or through official forms and documents from abroad,” Sutaj Estok continued. He believes that family law in Slovakia should stay “as it has been for centuries.” The left-nationalist Prime Minister Robert Fico had, during a visit to a registry office in June, stated that the registration of same-sex partnerships is not possible under Slovak law. The ban on marriage in the constitution was established in 2014 during a previous Fico government (TheColu.mn reported). EU against restricting family life The European Court of Justice (ECJ) ruled in November 2025 that an EU country must recognize a marriage concluded in another EU state (TheColu.mn reported). In the specific case, it involved a Polish man and a Polish-German man who had married in Germany in 2018. They sought to move to Poland and requested the rewriting of their marriage certificate in the Polish civil status registry. Polish authorities refused. In March, Poland’s Supreme Administrative Court subsequently ruled that marriages between same-sex couples concluded in another EU state must be recognized — though the Constitutional Court, under the previous government, had previously ruled against recognition (TheColu.mn reported). The ECJ had ruled at the time that the non-recognition of the marriage violated the couple’s rights, namely the freedom of movement and residence and the fundamental right to respect for private and family life. In Slovakia, a gay couple who had married in Austria tried to register in the Slovak registry — unsuccessfully. The two men announced they would challenge the “illegal behavior” and asked other same-sex couples not to leave the country, saying, “we must stand up to the intimidations.” The European Commission opened proceedings A constitutional amendment passed last year further restricted the rights of queer people, as most married couples are now allowed to adopt children, recognition of non-binary/intersex people became impossible, and gender-affirming procedures were made more difficult (TheColu.mn reported). The European Commission opened proceedings on this in November (TheColu.mn reported). Slovakia stands alongside Poland, Bulgaria, and Romania as one of the last EU states that do not allow same-sex marriages or registered partnerships. https://www.dw.com/en/nato-jets-shoot-do.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MbDj Lithuanian authorities published images of what they said were the charred remains of the drone Image: Lithuanian Army/Handout/REUTERS Advertisement A drone which entered Lithuanian airspace in the early hours of Tuesday morning was shot down by NATO fighter jets in between the cities of Vilnius and Kaunas, Lithuanian authorities have confirmed. Lithuania 's National Crisis Management Center (NKVC) said the drone most likely came from neighboring Belarus , an ally of Russia in its ongoing war against Ukraine , and was flying west when it was shot down by an Italian jet. Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda thanked the military alliance for its "swift response." "With Russia intensifying its aggression against Ukraine , such readiness is vital for our region," he wrote on social media. "Together with our NATO Allies, Lithuania will defend its airspace." Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said the NATO response sent "a clear message that NATO stands vigilant, committed, and ready." Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda thanked the NATO military alliance for its 'swift response' Image: Jouni Porsanger/Lehtikuva/REUTERS What do we know about the latest drone incident? Vilmantas Vitkauskas, head of the NKVC, told Lithuanian public broadcaster LRT that the drone most likely entered from Belarus and flew along the outskirts of populated areas for about 30 minutes before being intercepted. The Lithuanian armed forces published video from the ​site of the crash near the village of Pratkunai, close to Lithuania's second-largest city, Kaunas, and about 80 kilometers (50 miles) west of the capital, Vilnius. The footage showed debris scattered in grass. Some of the parts appeared to be made from wood ⁠and ​some appeared charred. The commander of the Lithuanian air force, Antanas Matutis, said that the drone had "likely" been carrying explosives. Lithuania: Was the drone from Russia or Ukraine? Officials have not indicated whether the drone was Russian or Ukrainian. While Russia has been launching almost daily drone and missile strikes against Ukraine since the start of its full-scale invasion over four years ago, Ukraine has also been responding with drone strikes of its own. Ukrainian drones, which often pass close to Lithuanian, Latvian and Estonian airspace en route to targets in northwestern Russia, have occasionally been jammed by Russian defenses and steered off course into NATO airspace. Fighter jets with the NATO ​Baltic Air Defense mission have patrolled the skies over Latvia, Lithuania and ​Estonia since the Baltic ‌countries joined the alliance in 2004. The mission's jets shot down stray Ukrainian drones over Estonia ​in May , ⁠and over Latvia in June and August. The Lithuanian military said Tuesday's incident marked the first time that a drone had been shot down in its airspace . The drone fell around around 80 kilometers (50 miles) west of the Lithuanian capital, Vilnius Image: Lithuanian Army/Handout/REUTERS How has NATO responded? Tuesday's incident came less than 24 hours after NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said that strikes "close to the alliance's territory" would drive the trans-Atlantic organization to increase its support for Ukraine. "Russia is growing increasingly reckless as it continues its terrible war against Ukraine," he said, adding that drone strikes and incursions near NATO territory showed Russian President Vladimir Putin 's "desperation" and "desire to sow fear and terror." On Tuesday, Poland , a NATO ally and neighbor of Lithuania, also announced "aviation operations" had commenced in its airspace "due to the activity of Russian Federation's jet-powered unmanned aerial vehicles conducting strikes on Ukrainian territory." These actions are of a "preventive nature" and are aimed at "securing airspace and its protection, especially in areas adjacent to threatened regions," said authorities in Warsaw. Germany 's armed forces, the Bundeswehr , are also currently building up a German armored brigade in Lithuania . The combat-ready and independently deployable force, comprising 4,800 troops, is expected to be operational by 2027. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwvg.text: Image source, Getty Images By Aleks Phillips Published 14 November 2026, 10:30 GMT Updated 1 hour ago US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, Volodymyr Zelensky has said. The Ukrainian president's comments on Saturday come after US envoys visited Moscow and an EU summit in Dublin as part of ongoing efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine. Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance as a condition of any peace deal to deter future threats, while Russia has said another Nato member on its border was unacceptable. Zelensky has also consistently said Ukraine was unwilling to give up sovereign territory, despite Moscow's demands for it to cede the Donbas. "The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky told reporters on Saturday. He went on to say that if he received a proposal that contained security guarantees, no constraints on Ukraine's military and funds to rebuild the country, he would put it to a referendum. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to the Irish capital on Thursday to meet Zelensky, after a round of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Comments by both Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia's position on the war has not shifted, and that Moscow's demands for territory and neutrality continue to far exceed what Ukraine is prepared to consider. Moscow has previously proposed limits on the size of Ukraine's military, territorial concessions and Kyiv's guaranteed neutrality as conditions of a peace deal. Ukraine has rejected these, arguing that such constraints would hamper its ability to stave off any future invasion. There have, however, been recent signs the two can find common ground: last month, US First Lady Melania Trump was able to broker a temporary ceasefire in the the Kherson region to allow for evacuations and aid deliveries. US officials had previously said that Ukrainian Nato membership was off the table. Zelensky said on Saturday that the US proposal made him believe that "Nato is back on the agenda". But he cautioned: "You have also heard Putin's signals, and this is an extremely difficult conversation." Russia currently occupies roughly a fifth of Ukrainian territory, including most of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions that compose the Donbas. Ceding the small portions of land Ukraine still controls there would be symbolically significant for Kyiv because it would constitute an acceptance of the Donbas being Russian. Zelensky has previously spoken of retaking Russian-controlled territory in four of Ukraine's regions, as well as the Crimean peninsula, which Moscow annexed in 2014. The latest round of talks come after a period of fraught relations between Kyiv and Washington over Ukrainian strikes on oil facilities deep inside Russia, which US President Donald Trump had asked Ukraine to pause to facilitate the supply of Russian diesel to ease global fuel prices, which have been rising since the US and Israel attacked Iran in February. Zelensky then accused US officials of limiting Ukraine's Starlink internet service , which it uses to co-ordinate defensive operations, while Trump said it was "time for Ukraine to get a new president" and called for fresh elections. Elections are suspended while Ukraine remains under martial law, but Zelensky has previously said he was willing to hold them within months of a peace deal being reached and would give up the presidency in exchange for Nato membership.
